nodes.name: Chosen Limit
nodes.statement: Let $F : J \to C$ be a functor. A \emph{chosen limit} for $F$ is a specified limit cone for $F$.
nodes.label: def:chosen-limit

nodes.name: Chosen Limit implies Limit
nodes.statement: If we have a chosen limit for a functor $F$, then $F$ has a limit.
assumptions: we have a chosen limit for a functor $F$
also_stated_at: Note that chosen limits are also limits in the sense of there existing a limit cone.
nodes.label: prop:chosen-limit-implies-limit

nodes.name: Proof of Chosen Limit implies Limit
nodes.statement_short: Direct: an inhabited set (a chosen limit cone) is nonempty (a limit exists).

nodes.name: Existence of limits implies chosen limit
nodes.statement: Under choice, the reverse also holds.
nodes.statement_short: Under the axiom of choice, if $F$ has a limit then it has a chosen limit.

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of limits implies chosen limit
nodes.statement: Classically, a nonempty set is inhabited.
nodes.statement_short: Classical choice: a nonempty set is inhabited.

nodes.name: Chosen Limits of Shape
nodes.statement: A category $C$ has \emph{chosen limits of shape} $J$ if every functor $F : J \to C$ has a chosen limit.
differentia: every functor $F : J \to C$ has a chosen limit
nodes.label: def:chosen-limits-of-shape

nodes.name: Chosen Finite Limits
nodes.statement: A category $C$ has \emph{chosen finite limits} if it has chosen limits of shape $J$ for every finite category $J$, i.~e.~ for every finite limit cone.
differentia: it has chosen limits of shape $J$ for every finite category $J$
nodes.label: def:chosen-finite-limits

nodes.name: Chosen Finite Products
nodes.statement_short: A category with a chosen binary product fan for every pair of objects and a chosen terminal object.
nodes.label: def:chosen-finite-products

nodes.name: Chosen Finite Products from Limits
nodes.statement: If a category $C$ has chosen finite limits, then it has chosen finite products.
assumptions: a category $C$ has chosen finite limits
also_stated_at: Note that our definition is compatible, so that a category with chosen finite limits in particular has an instance of chosen finite products.
nodes.label: lem:chosen-finite-products-from-limits

nodes.name: Proof of Chosen Finite Products from Limits
nodes.statement: We construct the limit cones for the pair and the terminal object.
nodes.statement_short: Construction: build the chosen limit cones for the pair functor and the empty functor.

nodes.name: Monoidal category
nodes.statement:
In a \emph{monoidal category} \(\mathcal{C}\), we can take the \emph{tensor product} of objects, \(X ⊗ Y\) and of morphisms \(f ⊗ g\).
The tensor product does not need to be strictly associative on objects,
but there is a specified \emph{associator}, \(α_{X Y Z} : (X ⊗ Y) ⊗ Z ≅ X ⊗ (Y ⊗ Z)\).
There is a tensor unit \(\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{C}}\),
with specified left and right \emph{unitor isomorphisms}
\(λ_X : \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{C}} ⊗ X ≅ X\)
and \(ρ_X : X ⊗ \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{C}} ≅ X\).

These associators and unitors satisfy the pentagon and triangle identities.
nodes.statement_short: A category with a tensor product of objects and morphisms, an associator and left/right unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle identities.
nodes.label: def:monoidal-category

nodes.name: Cartesian closed category
nodes.statement:
A category \(\mathcal{C}\) is \emph{cartesian closed} if it has finite products and every object is exponentiable.

  We define this as a monoidal closed category with respect to the cartesian monoidal structure.
nodes.label: def:cartesian-closed-category

nodes.name: Subobject Classifier
nodes.statement:
In a category $C$ with chosen finite limits, a chosen \emph{subobject classifier} consists of:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item An object $\Omega$
  \item A monomorphism $\text{true} : 1 \to \Omega$ 
  \item For every monomorphism $m : U \to X$, a unique assigned morphism $\chi_m : X \to \Omega$ (the \emph{characteristic morphism}) such that the square
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        U \ar[r] \ar[d, "m"'] & 1 \ar[d, "\text{true}"] \\
        X \ar[r, "\chi_m"'] & \Omega
      \end{tikzcd}\]
    is a pullback.
  \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: An object $\Omega$ with a mono $\text{true}:1\to\Omega$ such that every mono $m$ has a unique characteristic map $\chi_m$ making $m$ the pullback of true.
nodes.label: def:subobject-classifier

nodes.name: Elementary Topos
differentia: is cartesian closed for the inherited chosen finite products,
also_stated_at: An \emph{elementary topos} is a Cartesian closed category with finite limits and a subobject classifier.
nodes.label: def:elementary_topos

nodes.name: Natural Numbers Object
nodes.statement: In a topos $\mathcal{C}$, a \emph{natural numbers object} is an object $N$ with morphisms $0 : 1 \to N$ and $s : N \to N$ satisfying the appropriate universal property.
nodes.label: def:nno

nodes.name: Topos with NNO
nodes.statement: A topos equipped with a natural numbers object.
nodes.label: def:topos_with_nno
